newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Singapore's Lee urges Taiwan, China to talk.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Lee urges Taiwan, China to talk.

text.p: Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew urged Taiwan and China to resume long-suspended talks and Taipei to halt its bid for a seat in the United Nations, Taiwan's official Central News Agency reported on Saturday.

The continuous tensions between the two longtime rivals will hurt Taiwan as the economic situation has changed and Taiwan has less bargaining power than it had five years ago, Lee was quoted as saying.
Lee made the comments to a group of Taiwanese lawmakers during their recent visit in Singapore, the agency said.
"The two sides should resume talks as soon as possible under the 'one China' principle," Lee told the Taiwanese delegation.
"Subjects, such as joining the United Nations, that will cause tensions should be put aside temporarily," Lee said.
Taiwan and China, political rivals since a civil war split them in 1949, held a landmark meeting at a quasi-official level in Singapore in 1993 and a series of lower-level talks afterwards.

Such communications were suspended by an angry China since mid-1995 after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui's private but high-profile visit to the United States, seen by Beijing as a move to promote the island's independence from China.
Both governments in Taipei and Beijing say they want reunification, but under very different terms.

China says Taiwan is a Chinese province not entitled to foreign recognition while Taiwan insists that its 21 million people have the right to join internationa forums, including the United Nations, before reunification.
Beijing took China's U.N. seat from Taipei in 1971.
